_comment: HISTORY for the home page's milestone band, rendered by sync_site.py.  ⚠⚠ THE CURRENT QUESTION COUNT IS NOT IN THIS FILE ON PURPOSE. It comes from study.db through counts(), because a number that lives in two places drifts — which is the entire reason sync_site.py exists (on 2 Aug 2026 four hardcoded numbers were wrong at once). Put only PAST, DATED facts here; anything still moving belongs in the database.  ⚠ EVERY DATE BELOW WAS CHECKED AGAINST THE DATABASES, not remembered. Three of them were wrong on the first draft: the first real payment is 2 Aug (not 1 Aug), the 100th person arrived on 7 Aug (not 4 Aug), and the exam-family split was 6 Aug (not 13 Aug, which was the grand-test pool split). A milestone list is a public claim about the product's history and it is the cheapest thing in the world for a reader to check.  Verify with: MIN(ts) FROM attempts; first_seen ordered from users; MIN(ts) FROM processed_payments excluding test_payments.  ⚠ Keep 'note' short. This is a band on the home page, not the fixes log — what changed and why lives on fixes.html, and these two must not turn into the same page.  ⚠ NO USER NAMES, NO PERSONAL NUMBERS. 'the 100th person arrived' is fine; who they were is not.  ⚠⚠ 'SERVABLE' MEANS WHAT THE BOT CAN ACTUALLY SEND, and the milestone labels must use the same rounded-DOWN figure the site shows. study.db holds 3,811 rows but 35 image questions have no uploaded figure, so 3,776 are servable and the site says 3,700+. The first draft of the 14 Aug entry said 3,800+ — an overstatement a reader could catch, and precisely what sync_site.py exists to prevent. Never take a milestone number from a row count.  ⚠⚠ THESE NOTES ARE PUBLIC COPY, NOT A CHANGELOG. Say what a reader GETS, never how it was produced. The first draft said '500 INI-CET questions imported and explained by hand, and 73 figures redrawn from scratch so they are ours' — 'imported' exposes a pipeline, and 'so they are ours' advertises a provenance worry the reader did not have and implies the older figures were not. Nawar cut it. Process belongs on fixes.html; this band is only 'how far this has come'.
